findings.title: Equity identity guard is tautological as written
findings.detail: valuation.py build_valuation_mark assigns equity = cash + pos_value and on the next lines checks abs(equity - (cash + pos_value)) > 0.005 — the check compares the value to the exact expression it was just computed from, so it can never fire. It functions only as a tripwire against future refactors that decouple the assignment. No correctness impact in the audited code: the auditor's independent recomputation reproduced the published equity with diff 0.0 and the dashboard-side identity checks on strategy events are separate and live.
findings.recommendation: Optional future hardening: derive equity through an independent path (e.g. recompute from the emitted position_rows) so the guard has discriminating power.

findings.title: Valuation equity and strategy event equity use different price classes — delta equals cumulative slippage by design
findings.detail: Measured on the real ledger: strategy event equity (99954.17251398179) = cash + sum(signed_qty x decision-ref closes) where target weights +/-0.2 x start-of-rebalance equity net the ref-price book to exactly 0; valuation entries are the slipped fill prices, so valuation equity at entry marks = cash + 5.827486018214466. The difference is exactly the cumulative slippage book — economically consistent (entry unrealized on each leg shows the slippage drag), cash is bit-for-bit identical in both surfaces, and the dashboard renders strategy equity and valuation equity in separate sections with their own disclosed identities. No conflation found.
findings.recommendation: None required; documentation already discloses the identity. Optionally state the price-class difference in the dashboard valuation section note.

findings.title: Boundary-crossing worker runs legitimately append new marks

Same-window idempotency was separately proven at append level (skip-on-existing) and at whole-worker level (two rapid runs: mark files byte-identical, marks_written 0, skipped_existing 6).
